clue.text: Imagine daughter touching cat's back

parts.note: touching means concerning, which is RE

indicators.note: back tells us the big cat's name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a puma is a big cat; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone pictures their daughter stroking the cat along its spine.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream something up is to invent or conjure it in the mind, a phrasal synonym for imagine.

clue.text: Almost comic live action hero

indicators.note: almost means the comic's title stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: The Dandy was a long-running British children's comic
live as in exist gives ARE (we are, we live)

explanation.surface: A nearly-funny live-action film hero is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy is a British children's comic; Dan Dare, pilot of the future, starred in the rival Eagle comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Dan Dare is the British comic-strip space pilot, a classic heroic adventure character.

clue.text: Maiden over of superior quality

parts.note: over in the sense of surplus or additional gives EXTRA
a maiden is a virgin

explanation.surface: A cricket over with no runs conceded is praised as top-class.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over is a cricket term for an over of six balls with no runs scored; here the words are split into two synonyms and placed in the answer's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra virgin describes the finest grade of olive oil, hence anything of top quality.

clue.text: I stand on this bunk!

definitions.meaning: read literally, the thing one personally stands on is one's own foot
bunk is nonsense, and the exclamation is a scornful dismissal of a claim

explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation scoffs at nonsense, like 'rubbish!', while literally naming the body part a person stands on.

clue.text: Big shot with mansion and a chauffeur

parts.note: a pile is a large stately house
a chauffeur is a hired driver

explanation.surface: A tycoon with a grand house and a uniformed chauffeur is pictured.
explanation.definitionFit: A piledriver is slang for a very powerful blow or shot in sport, such as a fierce kick.

clue.text: Inch quietly away from dust cloud following quake

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the quake word

parts.note: to quake is to shake or rock

indicators.note: away from means the quiet letter leaves the cloud word

parts.note: a pall is a dark cloud of dust or smoke
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone edges silently out of the dust raised by an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inch' looks like a verb of slow movement, but it is the Scottish word for a small island; Rockall is a tiny islet in the North Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland an inch is a small island, and Rockall is a lonely rocky islet.

clue.text: For audience, interpret a piece for organ

indicators.note: for audience means the word is to be taken as heard by listeners

parts.note: to interpret text is to read it

explanation.surface: A musician interprets a composition written for organ to listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a vibrating component in some organ pipes, so it is a part of the instrument.

clue.text: One taking snaps enjoys the flowers

parts.note: a crocodile, or croc, snaps its jaws
to enjoy a right is to use it, so enjoys gives USES

explanation.surface: A photographer delights in shooting the blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One taking snaps' suggests a photographer; it is the snapping crocodile.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocuses are small spring-flowering bulbs, an example of flowers.

clue.text: Drawing conclusions from ultra superior argument

indicators.note: conclusions from means the closing letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Someone concludes an extremely lofty debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing is one form of visual art, so the general term covers it.

clue.text: Old men swimming with energy daily across channel

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of the two words moving about freely

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Elderly men with plenty of energy swim the Channel every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges OLD MEN into LEMOND, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Monde is a French daily newspaper, published across the English Channel from Britain.

clue.text: Lover or partner to bolt food

definitions.meaning: an enthusiast or fan, as in a fitness fanatic
a threaded fastener paired with a bolt
an edible kernel in a hard shell

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a fanatic, the fastener screwed onto a bolt, and an edible kernel.

clue.text: Folding leaf's mechanical partition

indicators.note: folding suggests the letters being bent into a new arrangement

parts.note: Bottom is one of the 'rude mechanicals', the workmen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A table's folding leaf works as a mechanical divider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folding' rearranges LEAFS into FALSE; the possessive's S counts here as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A false bottom is a hidden panel dividing off a secret space in a box or case.

clue.text: A disadvantage going in with a cold-blooded killer

indicators.note: going in means the first pair of pieces enters the word for with

parts.note: with can mean and, as in bread with butter
a con is a disadvantage, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A handicap combined with a ruthless murderer is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold-blooded' hints at a callous murderer, but it means a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaconda is a huge constricting snake; reptiles are cold-blooded and it kills prey.

clue.text: US city organised workers zone in centre

parts.note: the TUC (Trades Union Congress) is Britain's body of organised workers, with the possessive S of workers' kept as a letter

indicators.note: in centre means only the middle letters of the zone word are used

explanation.surface: An American city's trade unionists occupy its downtown district.
explanation.walkthrough: The S comes from the possessive: the setter reads 'organised workers zone' as TUC's zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucson is a large city in Arizona, in the south-western United States.

clue.text: Standard charge to pen French that's appropriate

indicators.note: to pen means to enclose, so the French piece sits inside

parts.note: a set price is a standard or fixed one
que is French for that, plus the S of the contraction
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A fixed fee is charged for confining a suitable Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To sequestrate is to seize or confiscate property, a synonym of appropriate as a verb.

clue.text: Artist buzzing round China cut short a great show

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: round means the buzzing letters surround the next pieces

parts.note: a run of Zs represents a buzzing sound

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the friend word is dropped

parts.note: china means mate, from cockney rhyming slang china plate

explanation.surface: An artist hums around china shortened for a spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate (friend), cut short to MAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Razzmatazz is showy, noisy display, a lavish spectacle.

clue.text: Irishman seeing nothing odd in devotion

indicators.note: nothing odd in means the letters in odd positions are discarded, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: An Irishman finds no strangeness in religious fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: Eoin is the Irish form of the name John, borne by Irishmen.

clue.text: Resentment about worry's sort of novel

indicators.note: about means the resentment word goes around the worry

parts.note: pique is resentment from wounded pride
care is worry; the S here comes from worry's as 'worry is' read as plural CARES

explanation.surface: Someone resents a story's anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: A picaresque novel follows the episodic adventures of a roguish hero.

clue.text: Condition associated with elegance? Not quite

definitions.text: Condition associated with elegance? Not quite

parts.note: if introduces a condition

indicators.note: not quite means the elegance word loses its last letter

parts.note: finesse is refinement or elegance

explanation.surface: A state linked to stylishness is almost reached.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a state that is not quite the thing is dubious, iffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffiness is doubtfulness, the state of being uncertain or not quite right.

clue.text: With time, delivers sound anti-inflationary measure

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: sound means the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to deliver is to free or release

explanation.surface: Over time, someone hands out a sensible measure against rising prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage freeze holds pay steady to curb rising prices, a typical anti-inflation policy.

clue.text: Bats want to flourish, finally building stand

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters go wildly astray
finally means the last letter of the flourish word

explanation.surface: Bats want to thrive, eventually building a roost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the animals; it is crazy, signalling the rearrangement of WANT, TO and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is a Victorian stand with open shelves for displaying ornaments.

clue.text: With ink one's maybe filled in form

definitions.meaning: an inkwell is a pot filled with ink

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a hole holding liquid, as in an inkwell, and in good health.

clue.text: Yank, heading off, gets striking win, by chance

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to yank is to pluck or tug
workers out are on strike

explanation.surface: An American, setting off, scores a fortunate win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American (and luck out is a US phrase), but it means a tug.
explanation.definitionFit: To luck out is to succeed through good fortune, an American idiom.

clue.text: Humble and desperate measure again used in extremes

indicators.note: used in extremes means only the first and last letters of each word count

explanation.surface: A drastic measure is taken again in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower or humiliate them, a verb sense of humble.

clue.text: Broadcaster that's first-rate and free

parts.note: A, as in A1, means first-rate
to untie is to free

explanation.surface: A radio presenter is excellent and unconstrained.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Auntie is the affectionate nickname for the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster.

clue.text: Parent and kid about to pocket one grand

parts.note: ma is mother, a parent

indicators.note: to pocket means to enclose, so the one sits within

parts.note: to kid is to jest or joke
C (circa) means about
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mother and child are about to steal a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one grand' looks like a thousand pounds; 'grand' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means imposing and stately, a synonym of grand.

clue.text: Capable of working at till

definitions.meaning: equal to a task, as in not feeling equal to it
busy with, as in what are you doing
until, as in up until a time

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means equal to a task, engaged in doing something, and until.

clue.text: Feeling less pressure, once Reg is here

parts.note: more numb means feeling less
P is the physics symbol for pressure
late means former, once

explanation.surface: Someone under less stress is relieved now that Reg has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Reg is short for registration; British car number plates are known by their registration.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's registration mark is displayed on its number plate.

clue.text: Press dismiss second book of mine, then reflect

indicators.note: reflect means the result is mirrored, read backwards
dismiss second means drop the second of the two book letters

parts.note: a mine is an explosive device, a bomb

explanation.surface: The media sack the second volume of an author's memoir, then ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: Press means a crowd or throng, as does mob.

clue.text: Some tea? Don't bother!

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A host offers tea and the guest declines politely.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or trouble, a synonym of bother as a noun.

clue.text: Strike's backing so firm in Mexican province

indicators.note: backing means the strike word reads in reverse

parts.note: to bat is to strike; the possessive adds no letter
as means so, as in as good
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A strike gets a firm's support in a Mexican region.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a state of Mexico on the Gulf coast, a federal province.

clue.text: Bananas, more than anything, in a turnover stopping appetite!

indicators.note: stopping means the turned piece plugs the appetite word

parts.note: zest is keen appetite or relish

indicators.note: turnover means the letters are flipped round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bananas in a pastry turnover put someone off food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit, and 'turnover' like a pastry; bananas means crazy here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas means crazy, and the most crazy is the zaniest.
